status_note: active but non-functional: all three AI routes (gen-ai-code, ai-chat, enhance-prompt) are stubbed to HTTP 503 with a 'ponytail: AI generation disabled' comment; derivative of Ratna-Babu/Ai-Website-Builder (same package name project_doomsday, same file layout, LICENSE credits it)
core_problem: Chat-to-React-site tutorial clone: user types a prompt, the model returns a JSON map of Vite/React files, Sandpack renders them in the browser, JSZip exports them. In this fork the actual model calls have been removed.
architecture: Next.js 15 App Router (JS, not TS). data/Prompt.jsx holds three string prompts (CHAT_PROMPT persona, CODE_GEN_PROMPT, ENHANCE_PROMPT_RULES). components/custom/CodeView.jsx builds the request as `JSON.stringify(messages) + Prompt.CODE_GEN_PROMPT` (entire chat history serialised as a JSON string and concatenated to the instructions, composed on the client) and POSTs to app/api/gen-ai-code/route.jsx, which now returns 503. The expected contract is a JSON object {projectTitle, explanation, files:{'/App.js':{code}}, generatedFiles[]}; the client reads SSE 'data:' lines, takes `finalData.files`, runs preprocessFiles (coerces strings/objects into {code}) and shallow-merges over Lookup.DEFAULT_FILE (public/index.html with cdn.tailwindcss.com, App.css, tailwind.config.js, postcss.config.js) with no validation. Preview is @codesandbox/sandpack-react template 'react' with externalResources ['https://cdn.tailwindcss.com'] and a customSetup.dependencies list (Lookup.DEPENDANCY) that includes firebase, @google/generative-ai, MUI, react-toastify, three uuid packages. Persistence is Convex with schema `workspace: {messages: v.any(), fileData: v.optional(v.any())}` (untyped blobs). Export writes the same files plus a synthesized package.json into a zip. Repo also commits .omc/ agent state, a vexp AGENTS.md, and a PERFORMANCE_IMPROVEMENTS.md about useCallback/dynamic imports.
core_innovation: None; it is a de-wired copy of a YouTube-tutorial Bolt clone whose only distinguishing artifact is a prompt that spells out the canonical AI-slop aesthetic as requirements.
strengths: The CODE_GEN_PROMPT is an unusually explicit written specification of the generic AI look (indigo-500/purple-500/pink-500 gradients, backdrop-blur glassmorphism, rounded-2xl, shadow-xl, hover:scale-105 / -translate-y-1, gradient text headlines, lucide icons, framer-motion) and therefore a useful seed corpus for a tier-1 token ban list.

ENHANCE_PROMPT_RULES example output ('deep purple (#1a1a2e) backgrounds and vibrant gradient accents (indigo to pink)... glassmorphism cards... glowing input focus states... subtle particle effects') is a second, copy-level list of clichés to ban.
Sandpack-in-browser preview with a fixed dependency allowlist is a cheap, working preview mechanism for React output (mechanism is Sandpack's, not the repo's).
weaknesses: AI generation is disabled: every API route returns 503, so the repo cannot be run as described; README tells users to restore configs/AiModel.jsx from git history, which the shallow default branch no longer contains.

Output contract is an untyped JSON files map parsed on the client with no schema, no dependency check, no build check; any model drift (App.jsx vs App.js, missing files) reaches Sandpack as a red error overlay.
System prompt is assembled client-side and the whole message history is stringified into the prompt, so any user can rewrite the instructions and cost is unbounded by history length.

Prompt hardcodes the slop aesthetic as mandatory ('Use gradient backgrounds (e.g., from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500)', 'Add subtle glassmorphism effects', 'Card hover lift effects'), and instructs the model to use 'https://images.unsplash.com/photo-[id]?w=800' URLs, which yields hallucinated photo ids and broken images.
Convex schema stores messages and files as v.any(); no versioning, no lineage, no telemetry.
Dependency hygiene: jszip and jzip, uuid + uuidv4 + uuid4, MUI alongside Tailwind, firebase and @google/generative-ai injected into every exported project's package.json.
Committed tooling residue (.omc state, .vscode/mcp.json, vexp AGENTS.md) indicates an agent-edited repo with no review; 11 stars, single author.
patterns_to_steal: Prompt text as ban-list corpus: harvest the literal class tokens and phrases from CODE_GEN_PROMPT and the ENHANCE example ('from-indigo-500 via-purple-500 to-pink-500', 'backdrop-blur', 'glassmorphism', 'hover:scale-105', 'hover:-translate-y-1', 'gradient text', 'particle effects', 'glowing', 'floating geometric shapes') → anti_slop tier-1 regex/token bans and tier-3 n-gram seed list.

Fixed dependency allowlist passed to the sandbox (Lookup.DEPENDANCY → Sandpack customSetup) → qa_gate: our Astro build should fail on any import outside a pinned allowlist, which is the deterministic version of this idea.
patterns_to_avoid: Client-composed system prompt with serialised chat history appended → prompt injection, unbounded token cost, and no server-side control of what the model is told; our pipeline keeps prompts server-side and the model only selects ids.
Untyped JSON files map as the AI-to-renderer contract → no Zod validation possible, no way to detect truncation or missing files; contradicts SiteDefinition typed contract.
Aspirational and aesthetic-prescriptive prompting ('visually stunning', 'impress users immediately', mandatory gradients/glassmorphism) → already rejected; this repo shows exactly what it produces.
Model-invented image URLs (unsplash photo-[id]) → violates asset_constraints on real photos; hallucinated ids render as broken images in front of a client.
v.any() persistence with no generation lineage → no telemetry, no priors promotion, no reproducibility.
reusable_patterns: SlopLexiconHarvest: mine tutorial-grade generation prompts for the literal utility classes and adjectives they mandate and turn them into a ban list.
SandboxDependencyAllowlist: preview environment is given a fixed, pinned dependency set so anything the model imports outside it fails loudly at preview time.
ScaffoldMergeDefaults: deterministic scaffold files are shallow-merged under model output so boilerplate never depends on the model (weak here because model files can still overwrite scaffold).
adoption_strategy: Ignore. There is no running generation path, no validation, no typed contract, and the prompt is a textbook example of the aesthetic we are building a gate against. The only durable value is the prompt text itself as a lexicon of slop tokens for the anti-slop engine; copy those strings into the tier-1 ban list and move on. Do not use the Sandpack setup as a reference either; our renderer is Astro and preview is a static build, not an in-browser bundler.
